page: Microsoft Azure E4as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores operating at up to 4.5 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 32 MB of Level 3 cache, 1.0 MB of Level 2 cache, and 48 KB of Level 1 data cache. Memory provisioning provides 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration features no local storage and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread capability, with stress-ng single-core execution scoring 3556.07 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 38.71 GB/sec, placing both in the top tier of tested hardware. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression registers at 17.73 GB/sec. Across multi-core tasks, stress-ng achieves an average score of 7164.89, while PassMark overall CPU reaches 9677.68. Memory bandwidth shows 46.13 GB/sec on uncached reads and 33.69 GB/sec on writes. In-memory data structures demonstrate solid throughput, evidenced by 7.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.77 GB/sec in static web serving.

The primary tradeoff of the E4as_v7 stems from its 2-core physical limit and absence of onboard ephemeral storage, which requires external storage attachments for disk-bound operations. Multi-threaded decompression and medium-sized LLM inference remain comparatively weak due to core count constraints. Qualitatively, the instance delivers high memory density per core alongside high single-core clock frequencies, making it a cost-efficient platform for medium-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data processing pipelines, and enterprise application hosting.
description: Microsoft Azure E4as_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores running on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor at 4.5 GHz. Configured with 32.0 GB of memory, it delivers an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, suitable for memory-intensive systems. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache, full AVX-512 vector support, no integrated GPU acceleration, and no local disk storage, necessitating remote volumes. Benchmark profiles show top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by strong stress-ng single-thread scores and high gzip compression speeds, alongside average multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth. Redis performance reaches 7.67 million SET operations per second. Due to its balanced memory density and high clock speeds, the E4as_v7 is well suited for in-memory caching layers, medium relational database workloads, and enterprise applications that do not depend on high core counts or integrated local NVMe storage.
